# Independent audit of the explicit all-cap escape point

The completed proof in `candidate 4a8c4181997d22b7`
passes independent audit, together with its scalar dependency
`candidate 191a0eb2244ea4a9`. No defect
was found. Both accompanying exact verifiers pass, and the strict
inequalities below were also recomputed separately with Fractions.

## 1. Scalar dependency

The conditional-mean MLR argument handles support zeros by cross-products,
not undefined ratios. Its nondecreasing conditional means sum to the
conditioning value, hence are 1-Lipschitz. The exponential Stein identity
has the same sign for positive and negative coefficients. It gives the
needed density derivative sign after adding the two positive exponential
phases. Exponential size bias and the positive-exponential convolution ODE
give the exact coefficient-derivative difference. Merging into a largest
coefficient preserves the required sign; arbitrary merging is neither
used nor valid. The zero-coefficient limits have no equality atom.

Full independent analytic details are in
`historical context (not an accepted premise)`. The scalar theorem
gives a simplex centroid-cap bound gamma_q in terms of the number q of
strictly negative vertices. Boundary vertices have zero affine values
and can be omitted in the exponential comparison.

## 2. Candidate, measure, and cap reduction

The displayed six barycentric coordinates are positive and sum to one.
Thus the candidate belongs to the actual middle fiber B. The ratio
1/5 in its first two coordinate displacements is strictly below the
wedge slope 9/2, proving that it is outside the failed selector hull.

Every original fiber is full five-dimensional. Its boundary hyperplanes
have zero five-volume, and H_5 on the mixed union is the sum of the
three fiber volumes. Dividing by |B| is common to every mass and target.

A nonvertical containing ambient halfspace can be shrunk through the
candidate. Because the candidate is interior to B, its trace has at
least one strictly positive and one strictly negative vertex margin.
Thus the one-positive and multiple-positive branches exhaust every such
trace, including any number of zero-margin boundary vertices.

## 3. One-positive-vertex branches

With the margin normalized to one at its positive vertex, the five edge
intercepts lie in (0,1]. The cap is the simplex with those edge points
and the positive vertex, so its volume is their product. Its through-point
constraint is the stated sum lambda_k/ell_k=1. AM--GM yields the exact
product lower bound; the equality intercepts 5 lambda_k are feasible.

The type-one branch gives gamma_5(1+2a), strictly above the target.
For a short intercept, the distinguished term is at least s_0>1/5.
The function s((1-s)/4)^4 is decreasing on [1/5,1), so the denominator
bound has the correct direction. Its exact cap lower bound exceeds
gamma_5(1+1/200000), which exceeds the actual target.

For the long-intercept branches, every B point has normalized margin
at least -3/7. Each applicable positive vertex index has a vertex w of
D whose corresponding barycentric coordinate is at least T. In particular
index zero uses b_0, index two can use the apex, and indices three through
five use their coordinate-shifted base vertices. This gives L(w)>1/2.
The smaller simplex D' has L>=15/56.

The affine scaling identity includes its constant term correctly:
the constants from sD and qD cancel because s+q=2. It yields

    min_A L+L(qx)>=9/22>0,       x in D'.

Hence every integer tilt either includes all of A or includes qD'.
The latter has relative volume 1/1024>a. The endpoint contribution is
therefore at least a; sufficiently negative tilt attains a exactly.
The resulting lower cap budget exceeds the target because

    1-(9/10)gamma_5-(16/5)gamma_5/100000>0.

This argument includes equality in endpoint inclusion inequalities and
does not discard supporting endpoint faces.

## 4. Multiple-positive-vertex branches

Let A_+,B_- be the positive and negative coefficient totals. The actual
barycentric through-point equation gives A_+/B_->=l/L, with no assumption
that the candidate is the centroid. If A_+>=B_-, coefficient scaling and
the scalar theorem immediately give the required lower bound.

Otherwise put r=B_-/A_+>1 and scale the k positive exponentials by r.
Their new joint density pointwise dominates r^(-k) times their old
density. Thus the common probability mass of the two laws is at least
r^(-k), and their total variation distance, in the event-supremum
convention, is at most 1-r^(-k). This justifies subtracting that quantity
from the balanced probability. The unchanged negative variables do not
increase total variation.

The sequence of bounds

    1-(A_+/B_-)^k<=k(1-A_+/B_-)
                   <=5(1-l/L)<=12a

is correct. There are at most four strictly negative vertices, so the
balanced comparison is at least gamma_4. Separately recomputed arithmetic
gives

    gamma_4-12/100000-gamma_5(1+1/200000)
                         =3940057/518400000>0.

Therefore the middle fiber alone exceeds the target for every
multiple-positive-vertex trace. Boundary vertices only reduce the number
of positive or negative phases and do not invalidate this argument.

## 5. Remaining orientations and scope

A vertical containing halfspace contains all of B and has relative mass
at least one, strictly above the target. All nonvertical orientations
were exhausted by the preceding branches, and arbitrary integer tilts
were retained throughout.

The result is consequently an exact all-halfspace center certificate for
the fixed n=1,d=5 selector-obstruction body. It demonstrates that the
failed selector can be escaped by an actual point of S. It is not a
claim for arbitrary bodies or a resolution of OC.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
